ordered_diagnoses: Pleomorphic adenoma of the facial nerve

facts.raw_span: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis
denied hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
complete right facial paralysis
nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz
5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen
heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
expansion of the stylomastoid foramen
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67
Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a diagnosis of facial nerve schwannoma, a type of benign tumor that arises from the Schwann cells of the facial nerve.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could also be consistent with a diagnosis of facial nerve hemangioma, a type of benign vascular tumor that can occur in the facial nerve.
The patient's imaging findings and pathology results could also suggest a diagnosis of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor, a type of malignant tumor that arises from the nerve sheath.
The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could also be consistent with a diagnosis of facial nerve neurofibroma, a type of benign tumor that arises from the nerve tissue.

The patient's imaging findings and pathology results could also suggest a diagnosis of chondrosarcoma of the temporal bone, a type of malignant tumor that arises from the cartilage of the temporal bone.
